draft.title: Rhetorical devices in speeches
card: Group of three
three words, phrases or ideas in a row, such as "we must listen, learn and act". The rhythm feels complete and is easy to remember.
Repetition
the same word or phrase at the start of lines, such as "We will not give up. We will not step back." It builds force and drives a point home.
Contrast
two opposite ideas placed side by side, such as "small steps, giant change". It makes a point sharper and clearer.
Direct address
speaking straight to the audience with words like you, we and us, such as "You can change this school". It makes listeners feel included and involved.
draft.remember: Speakers use these devices to make ideas stick in the ears and minds of listeners.

a.q: A student captain tells her school: "We came, we worked, we won." Which device is this?
opts: Repetition at the start of lines
a.why: The line has three short actions in a row, which is a group of three. It is not repetition at the start of lines, because the actions are what build the rhythm, not one repeated opening phrase. There are no opposite ideas, so it is not contrast.
a.clue: Count the actions in the line.

b.q: Jaya opens three lines in a row with the same words, "You hold the power to", and then ends them with clean, protect and save. Which device gives the speech its main force, and what is its effect?
opts: Repetition at the start of lines, which builds force
Contrast, which sets two opposite ideas side by side
A group of three, which makes each line feel complete
Direct address, which makes listeners feel left out
b.why: The same phrase opens each line, so this is repetition at the start of lines, and it builds force. The word you is direct address too, but that device makes listeners feel included, not left out. There are no opposite ideas, so it is not contrast.
b.clue: Look at how each line begins.

b.best: Repetition at the start of lines, which builds force

Contrast

Direct address

proposal.remember: Speakers use these devices to make ideas stick in the ears and minds of listeners.

a.q: A council speaker says: "This new park offers shade, space and peace." Which device is this?
opts: Repetition at the start of lines
a.why: Shade, space and peace are three things listed in a row, so this is a group of three. It is not repetition at the start of lines, because no opening word or phrase is repeated across lines. There are no opposite ideas and no words like you or we, so it is not contrast or direct address.
a.clue: Count the things the speaker lists.

b.q: Jaya is giving a speech about rubbish in the school yard. She wants each listener to feel the problem is theirs to fix. Which device suits this aim best?
opts: Repetition at the start of lines
b.why: Direct address speaks straight to the audience with words like you and we, which makes listeners feel included and involved. Repetition at the start of lines builds force, but it does not on its own speak to the listeners or draw them in.
b.clue: Which device brings the listener into the speech?
